newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bonds mixed in dull market, no change seen.
newsitem.headline: Danish bonds mixed in dull market, no change seen.

text.p: Danish bond prices were mixed on Monday in a dull market becalmed by closed bourses in London and New York, with dealers seeing little movement ahead.
"After falling on the left-wing victory in the French election's first round, nothing much has happened and little more is expected to happen today," one dealer said.

The benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 was up 0.06 point from the opening at 110.10 yielding 6.45 percent in turnover of 1.1 billion crowns while the forthcoming seven percent 2007 benchmark was 0.36 point down at 102.90 in 300 million crown turnover yielding 6.59 percent.
The 2006 benchmark's June future fell 0.12 point to 109.88 with 129 contracts traded. The six percent mortgage bond due 2026 lost 0.25 point to 88.50.
The crown traded at 3.8085 per mark at 1140 gmt, unchanged from the opening.
The yield gap between the 2006 bond and the German bund narrowed three points to 53 basis points and the 2007-bund gap narrowed by the same margin to 68 bp.
